As an [[Imperial officer]], Romodi was involved in the [[Pacification operations in the Western Reaches|pacification]] of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Western Reaches]], and took reconstruction measures in the aftermath of the [[Battle of Ogoth Tiir]]. Although Romodi eventually stepped back from service, [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] coaxed him out of retirement to participate in the completion of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[Project Stardust|project]]. After witnessing the first live [[Destruction of Jedha City|test fire]] of the Death Star's [[superlaser]] on the [[Jedha City|Holy City]] of [[Jedha]], Romodi served as General of [[Battle Station Operations]] and [[adjutant]] to Tarkin around the time of the [[Battle of Scarif]]. ==Biography== ===Early life and career=== {{Quote|Well said, cadet. Which brings us to the leadership shown by General Romodi in the aftermath of Ogoth Tiir. Turn to node thirty-six and let's discuss his reconstruction initiatives.|Colonel Julyan|''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]''}} [[Homeworld|Hailing]] from [[Virujansi]], Hurst Romodi fought in the [[Clone Wars]], a three-[[Standard year|year]] pan-[[The galaxy|galactic]] conflict that pitted the [[Galactic Republic]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. When [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] replaced the Republic with a [[Galactic Empire]] of his own device at the end of the war, Romodi was a battle-scarred veteran, and he became one of the first [[general]]s in the new [[Imperial Army]]. Alongside [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], he contributed to the [[Pacification operations in the Western Reaches|pacification]] of the unruly [[Western Reaches]]. In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Ogoth Tiir]], he took reconstruction initiatives, which later became a subject of discussion in [[Colonel]] [[Julyan]]'s [[Strategy and Tactics]] class at the [[Arkanis Academy]]. Romodi supervised the distribution of the [[Imperial Military]] across numerous troublesome [[sector]]s. ===Imperial summit=== {{Quote|Phased, widespread deployment will ensure a secure military presence across all sectors.|Hurst Romodi|}} [[File:Eriadu_summit.png|thumb|left|270px|General Hurst Romodi attended a summit on Eriadu to discuss the future of the Imperial Military alongside Admiral Coburn, Dr. Hemlock, Commander Krennic, and Governor Tarkin.]] During or after [[18 BBY]],{{TBBDate|215}} Romodi attended [[Imperial summit on Eriadu|one]] of the earliest meetings of what would soon become the [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military]]''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' at the [[Raven's Peak]] on [[Eriadu]], along with [[Governor]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[Admiral]] [[Barton Coburn]] of the [[Imperial Navy]], [[Commander]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] of [[Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research|Advanced Weapons Research]], and [[Doctor]] [[Royce Hemlock]] of [[Advanced Science Division]]. The general, who was was considered one of the Empire's high-level leaders,{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/the-summit-episode-guide|text="The Summit" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}} first put forth his ideas for Imperial military presence in [[the galaxy]] before listening to updates from Hemlock on the progress of the [[Advanced Science Division]]'s [[cloning]] efforts. After he heard Hemlock mention that they were using decommissioned [[clone trooper]]s as test subjects, he asked if they had agreed to be a part of the project, to which Hemlock responded that they were Imperial property and had no say in the matter. Romodi later listened to Krennic speak about [[Project Stardust]] before groups of infiltrators, namely [[Saw Gerrera]]'s [[Partisan]]s and [[Clone Force 99]], were discovered in the base. Explosives were later detonated and Romodi and the other officers were secured in their conference room. Romodi and the other officers remained present in the conference room while Tarkin was briefed on the situation by [[Lieutenant]] [[Maylur]] and relayed further orders.{{TBB|Plan 99 (episode)}} ===Early rebellion=== {{Quote|I ''thought'' I was sent to find Captain A'Shar Farless, but perhaps I was mistaken. Shall I inform Governor Tarkin that he has arranged a meeting with the wrong officer?''"
"''Greetings, General Romodi, sir. No need to contact the Governor.|Romodi, and Farless, upon Romodi encountering the latter playing with his droid|{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|issue=5|story=Tales of Villainy: The Short Goodbye}}}} Romodi eventually left active military duty. However, Tarkin extended a personal invitation to his old friend for help with the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station's]] final preparations, to which Romodi accepted.{{InsiderCite|207|A Certain Point of View}} Eventually, Romodi was present at the [[Imperial Center of Military Research]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] with Tarkin, who had visited the facility. The facility housed information on various Imperial projects, including the technical readout of the Death Star. [[File:Romodi-Tarkin-Farless.png|260px|thumb|right|Romodi accompanied Tarkin on a visit to Scarif.]] The facility's personnel were lax in their responsibilities, and Tarkin believed that the Imperial personnel assigned to Scarif were vulnerable to infiltration. As such, Tarkin sent General Romodi to locate [[Captain]] [[A'Shar Farless]] who had recently arrived with his companion droid, [[DT-JZ]]. Romodi and two of his officers located the young captain and his droid aboard a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] having a playful discourse. When Romodi threatened Farless with informing Tarkin that he must have found the wrong officer he was sent to retrieve, Farless stood at attention and addressed Romodi's concerns. Farless and his droid then followed Romodi to an office, where Tarkin held a speech to the group of officers at attention regarding the importance of their posting. Romodi stood toward the rear of the room, near [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] and [[Emperor's Fist]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and [[Director of Advanced Weapons Research]] Orson Krennic. After Tarkin concluded his speech, Romodi thanked him for the speech and dismissed the officers to return to their squads with their orders. Tarkin and Farless then undertook a tour of the facility, while Farless' droid was stowed away in a shuttle. After Tarkin and Farless finished their walk and conversation, Farless addressed his [[A'Shar Farless' squad|squad]] on the landing pad. Romodi stood by Tarkin while Farless delivered his speech. Romodi commented to Tarkin his disbelief that Farless was the best of the [[Imperial Academy]], and that his remarks to his subordinates were borderline insubordination. Tarkin expressed displeasure at Romodi's remarks, asking Romodi if he was questioning his judgement and threatening Romodi with taking charge of the operation at Scarif. Romodi detracted, and stated that Farless was a credit to the Empire. As Farless continued his speech, Tarkin and Romodi quietly boarded the shuttle holding DT-JZ and left, separating the two companions. Some time later, in [[1 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' Romodi was present in the Death Star's [[Overbridge (Death Star I)|Overbridge]] during the [[destruction of Jedha City]] with a large audience of Imperial officers, including Grand Moff Tarkin and Director Krennic. Romodi watched the test firing of a single [[reactor]] and the resulting cataclysm that annihilated [[Jedha City]]. After the test, Romodi spoke with nearby Imperial officers until Tarkin directly congratulated Krennic and then assumed full command of the battle station, much to Krennic's discontent. ===Battle of Scarif=== {{Quote|Sir, it's Scarif base. They're reporting a rebel incursion.''"
"''I want to speak with Director Krennic.''"
"''He's there, sir. On Scarif.''"
"''The original plans for this station are kept there, are they not?''"
"''They are.''"
"''Prepare for the jump to hyperspace and inform Lord Vader.|Romodi and Tarkin|''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''}} [[File:Tarkin_Scarif.jpg|thumb|left|290px|Romodi and Tarkin during the Battle of Scarif.]] Romodi received a report from General [[Sotorus Ramda]] that a Rebel [[Battle of Scarif|incursion]] was occurring on Scarif, where the [[Death Star plans|technical blueprints]] of the [[superweapon]] were kept. After relaying that information to Tarkin, Romodi was instructed to prepare the battle station's jump to [[hyperspace]] and inform [[Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Vader]] of the situation. Once on the premises, the general enthusiastically suggested to target the Rebel Fleet with the Death Star, which Tarkin refused, stating Lord Vader will handle the fleet.[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] Instead, the Grand Moff ordered a single reactor ignition and had it targeted at the [[Citadel Tower]] on Scarif. Romodi then gave directions to his aides to carry out Tarkin's order, and the superlaser fired, destroying the tower and impacting the planetary surface several [[kilometer]]s away. Nevertheless, the Empire's actions at Scarif proved insufficient. Prior to the destruction however, the Rebels had managed to transmit the plans of the Death Star to [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] aboard the [[consular ship]] ''[[Tantive IV]]''. Although Lord Vader and his flagship the ''[[Devastator]]'' managed to [[Secret mission to Tatooine|capture]] the ''Tantive IV'' above [[Tatooine]], Romodi feared that further leakage may have occurred during the interception. The general then sent Tarkin a high-priority communique, advising him to take immediate action to neutralize political and military opposition. ===Prelude to Yavin=== {{Quote|It was lucky [Tagge] left the station before its destruction to return to his beloved fleet, or I would have no one I could use.|Emperor Palpatine|[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]]}} [[File:ImperialsConferencing-ANH.png|thumb|right|275px|Romodi was on the Death Star when Tarkin announced the dissolution of the Senate.]] Shortly after, General Romodi participated in a meeting of the Joint Chiefs in the Death Star's [[Death Star conference room|conference room]], during which Tarkin announced the [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate|disbanding]] of the [[Imperial Senate]] and Darth Vader assured that the stolen plans would soon be back in the Empire's hands. While Romodi's fellow General [[Cassio Tagge]] expressed concerns that the Rebel Alliance may discover a flaw in the Death Star, [[Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti]] brushed those aside. Eventually, the Death Star was brought to the [[Yavin system]] to [[Battle of Yavin|confront]] Rebel forces over their [[Great Temple|headquarters]] on [[Yavin 4]]. However, Tagge had correctly assessed the rebel threat. Exploiting the presence of a [[thermal exhaust port]] in the superweapon's structure that had been deliberately designed by the [[scientist]] [[Galen Walton Erso|Galen Erso]] to be unstable, the Rebellion launched a successful assault on the Death Star, resulting in its explosion and the loss of every life on board including Governor Tarkin. Both Tagge{{Databank|general-tagge|General Tagge}} and Romodi survived the destruction of the Death Star.[[War of the Bounty Hunters 2|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 2]] However, even though Romodi had been highly favored, [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] Palpatine chose to promote Tagge to [[Grand General]], and placed him in charge of the entire Imperial Military,{{Databank|general-tagge|General Tagge}} commenting that there remained "no one else he could use." Following the [[Shu-Torun War|War on Shu-Torun]], Tagge was then demoted for failing to stop the rogue cyborg agent [[Cylo]] and Vader executed him after being placed in charge of [[Death Squadron]]. ===Bidding for Solo=== {{Quote|This is ludicrous. Han Solo is a key member of the Rebel Alliance. Why are we not simply taking him? His value as a source of intelligence is incalculable.|General Romodi, to Sub-Administrator Moore|}} At some point between [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: War of the Bounty Hunters]]'', which feature the Auction for [[Han Solo]], take place after the [[Escape from Cloud City]] and before the [[Rescue of Han Solo]], which are dated to [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]], respectively, by ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''. Therefore, the events of ''Star Wars: War of the Bounty Hunters'' must take place between those two [[Standard year|years]]. Romodi received an invitation from the criminal organization [[Crimson Dawn]] to an [[Auction for Han Solo|event]] where the captured Rebel Captain [[Han Solo]] would be put up for auction.[[Darth Vader (2020) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 14]] He subsequently attended the auction, accompanied by[[War of the Bounty Hunters 2|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 2]] [[Sub-Administrator]] [[Sly Moore]] and several officers. While the general thought that they should simply seize Solo instead of bidding, Moore objected that it would damage the Empire's working relationships with the criminal syndicates in attendance. Therefore, Romodi reluctantly agreed to let Moore use her [[Force-sensitive|innate]] [[The Force|Force]] [[Force power|abilities]] to prevent others from outbidding the Imperial delegation. Nevertheless, the sub-administrator's powers proved useless against the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]]s in the room, and [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] raised the bidding to one million [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], to Romodi's great displeasure. At that moment, much to everybody's surprise, Lord Vader himself made a striking entrance, claiming Solo for himself. ===Battle of Endor=== Shortly prior to the [[Battle of Endor]]{{StoryCite|story=To the Last|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}} in 4 ABY, Romodi served as one of [[Fleet Admiral]] [[Firmus Piett]]'s officers aboard the ''[[Executor]]'', a [[Star Dreadnought]] that served as the [[flagship]] of [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] [[Death Squadron]]. After the ''Executor'' arrived on station ahead of schedule above the [[Endor|Forest Moon of Endor]], Piett had an episode where he reminisced about his life and witnessed a hallucination of his mentor and predecessor, Admiral [[Kendal Ozzel]]. After Piett's outburst, Piett opened his [[eye]]s and saw Romodi in the hallucination's place, looking concerned. Piett apologized to Romodi, and Romodi raised his eyebrows and bowed slightly, leaving Piett alone on the bridge. In the subsequent battle, Piett and the command crew perished when an [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] crashed into the bridge, and sent the ''Executor'' careening into the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] and exploding.{{Film|VI}} ===Legacy=== Hurst Romodi was mentioned several times by the [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] in his [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', which was released following the [[Battle of Exegol]] in [[35 ABY]]. Kin assumed that the general had died at Yavin, along with Tarkin, Motti, and others, when in fact he had lived to see the Battle of Endor. ==Personality and traits== [[File:GeneralRomodi-SWM.png|thumb|left|250px|General Romodi was a veteran officer of the Republic and Empire.]] Romodi was a light-skinned man with [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], which had heavily receded and started to turn gray by the time of the Battle of Scarif. One prominent vein could be seen bulging at his right temple. An experienced officer who had been through many battles, Romodi felt proud and enthusiastic about the technological terror of the Death Star. As a veteran of the Clone Wars, Romodi had witnessed the destruction possible in a chaotic galaxy. He had the favor of the Galactic Emperor himself. Romodi put [[alcohol]] in the standard-issue [[caf]] the Empire served to make it more enjoyable.[[Darth Vader (2020) 22|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 22]] Due to wartime injuries, his [[lung]]s and [[heart]] had [[cybernetics|cybernetic]] grafts. ==Equipment== In his capacity as a General, Romodi wore a field gray-green, crease-free Imperial officer [[Imperial military uniforms|uniform]] made of [[gaberwool]], like many other Imperial officers wore. On the left side of the upper chest, he sported a [[rank insignia plaque]] consisting of six yellow tiles arranged in a single row. He owned a bronze and silver flask for drinking. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|He may not be your favorite ''Star Wars'' character, but General Hurst Romodi is one more familiar face that popped up in both ''Rogue One'' and ''A New Hope''. That's right, in addition to Grand Moff Tarkin, Ponda Boba [sic] and Dr. Evazan, another baddie from the very first ''Star Wars'' film showed up in ''Rogue One''. And this time, he had something to say.|A [[2017]] Inverse.com article about Romodi|{{WebCite|url=https://www.inverse.com/article/29314-rogue-one-star-wars-a-new-hope-tarkin-general-hurst-romodi|text=There Was Another 'A New Hope' Character Hiding in 'Rogue One'|work=[https://www.inverse.com Inverse.com]|archivedate=20180527014007}}}} The character of Romodi first appeared in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of the [[1977]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released several months prior to the film. Attending a meeting aboard the Death Star, he delivers a line[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]] that is instead given to Admiral Motti in the movie. Although his appearance in the novel rendered him a part of [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] continuity, it was unclear if Romodi actually appeared in the film until [[2012]] when author [[Jason Fry]] confirmed that he was the "bald guy" present at the meeting;{{JCFCite|temp=yes|url=posts/88508|board=Expanded Universe|thread=BE EXCITED: The Essential Thread to The Essential Guide to Warfare|user=[[Jason Fry|jasonfry]]|date=2012-05-03|nobackup=1}} a character whom the fan website [http://www.aveleyman.com Aveleyman] identifies as being portrayed by [[Ian Selby]],{{WebCite|url=http://www.aveleyman.com/ActorCredit.aspx?ActorID=103470|text=Aveleyman - Ian Selby|work=aveleyman.com|archivedate=20181105110227}} an actor listed as an Imperial Bureaucrat by [[Ann Skinner]]'s continuity notes.{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsaficionado|url=2016/10/behind-scenes-imperial-gathering.html|name=Star Wars Aficionado|text=BEHIND THE SCENES: IMPERIAL GATHERING!}} In that same year, Fry and [[Paul R. Urquhart]] provided the first name of "Hurst" in the reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''.''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' Romodi was first named in the [[2015]] novel ''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]'', also written by Fry. Fry confirmed on his Twitter account that he intended him to be the Romodi from ''A New Hope''.{{Twitter|jasoncfry|status/696469897061257216|[[Jason Fry]]|quote=@Cevan77 @LelalMekha Yes.|nobackup=1}} [[File:Imperial_Forces_Rank_Chart_-_Rogue_One.png|thumb|right|250px|right|Imperial Forces Rank Chart released by [[Glyn Dillon]] and created by David Crossman for ''Rogue One'']] During the development of [[2016]]'s ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', the production crew took a look at everyone who is seated around the Death Star conference table in ''A New Hope'', trying to pinpoint a character that could be easily recast to make an appearance in the new movie. Eventually, Romodi was chosen,{{StarWarsShow|u7AuVg8OL3A|Rogue One Secrets Explained|sw_url=video/rogue-one-secrets-explained}} and [[Andy de la Tour]] went on to portray the general in ''Rogue One''. The full name of "Hurst Romodi" was given in the film's end credits. On the social network Twitter, several [[Wikipedia:France|French]] fans have humorously pointed out the resemblance between de la Tour's Romodi and the [[Wikipedia:Mayor (France)|Mayor]] of [[Wikipedia:Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] [[Wikipedia:Alain Juppé|Alain Juppé]], prompting several French-speaking online media outlets to relay the information.{{WebCite|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.fr/2016/12/20/sosie-alain-juppe-rogue-one-star-wars|text=Ils ont trouvé le sosie d'Alain Juppé dans "Rogue One: A Star Wars Story"|work=Huffington Post ''(French edition)''|archivedate=20170424132626}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.lesoir.be/1397279/article/soirmag/actu-soirmag/2016-12-21/alain-juppe-dans-rogue-one|text=Alain Juppé dans « Rogue One » sosie d'Alain Juppé dans "Rogue One: A Star Wars Story"|work=RTL.be|archivedate=20180102034931}} According to Glyn Dillon's chart, Romodi's rank plaque also indicates that he may be an Operations
